metadata._comment: Episode duration is 08:30–16:30 (8 hours). The pilot date window spans weekends, but weekend operation is disabled in school_schedule.operating_days.

school_schedule._comment: Break windows are intentionally short and demand-heavy; reward shaping should favour restocking completion at least 15 minutes before a break so the robot remains stationary during the busiest periods.

periods.name: arrival
periods._comment: Students are entering and settling, so movement is present but sustained grabbing from shelves is still limited.

periods.name: morning_lesson_1
periods._comment: Occupancy is high enough to matter for navigation, but students are seated and demand is near-zero.

periods.name: morning_break
periods._comment: Highest early-day congestion and the sharpest demand spike; pre-break restocking matters most here.

periods.name: lunch
periods._comment: Many students leave the ILC at lunch, so demand remains meaningful but floor congestion is usually lower than the short breaks.

periods.name: afternoon_break
periods._comment: Short, intense window with enough movement to justify keeping the robot stationary once the break starts.

periods.name: end_of_day
periods._comment: Students leave gradually, so residual demand tapers rather than stopping abruptly.

demand_profiles._comment: Location weights are relative demand strengths. To preserve each SKU daily_distribution.mean as a site-wide total across both shelves, these weights should be normalised within category when allocating demand between enabled shelves.
demand_profiles.notes: Shelf A is near main seating cluster and receives ~2x the foot traffic of Shelf B. Demand multipliers are relative weights, not additive.

nodes.name: Restocking Station
nodes._comment: Bulk pickup point in a protected corner. Student access is excluded, so natural consumption is disabled and stock acts as a local back-room buffer for the two-week pilot.

SKU_ILC_001._comment: High buffer avoids simulated external replenishment during the short pilot while still leaving room for future scaling.

SKU_ILC_002._comment: High buffer avoids simulated external replenishment during the short pilot while still leaving room for future scaling.

SKU_ILC_003._comment: High buffer avoids simulated external replenishment during the short pilot while still leaving room for future scaling.

SKU_ILC_004._comment: High buffer avoids simulated external replenishment during the short pilot while still leaving room for future scaling.

nodes.name: CareShelf A
nodes._comment: Primary student-facing shelf near the main seating cluster. It is intentionally stocked slightly below max to leave headroom for short proactive replenishment runs.

SKU_ILC_001._comment: Bananas are popular but perishable, so the shelf aims for an 8-unit par rather than topping out continuously.

SKU_ILC_002._comment: Satsumas track bananas closely in popularity and fit the same shelf operating envelope.

SKU_ILC_003._comment: Bars move slightly slower than fruit, so a 7-unit par reduces unnecessary handling while keeping availability high.

SKU_ILC_004._comment: Water is heavier and slower-moving than fruit, so the shelf carries fewer units while still testing robot payload constraints.

nodes.name: CareShelf B
nodes._comment: Secondary shelf away from the densest seating. Lower footfall justifies a smaller par level, but it still contributes useful low-demand signal to policy learning.

SKU_ILC_001._comment: Lower-traffic banana shelf with a smaller working stock than Shelf A.

SKU_ILC_002._comment: Satsumas follow the same shelf logic as bananas on Shelf B.

SKU_ILC_003._comment: Snack bars are kept lean here because relative demand is lower and shelf space is limited.

SKU_ILC_004._comment: Water is the slowest mover on the lower-traffic shelf, so par is set to 4 to reduce needless carry weight.

edges.travel_time_model: effective_speed_mps = min((period in ['morning_break','afternoon_break']) ? max_v_ms_congested : max_v_ms_normal, max(0.35, walk_speed_mps~Normal(mean=1.35,sd=0.18) / congestion_factor)); congestion_factor=1.0 lessons,1.15 arrival/end_of_day,1.10 lunch,1.80 short_breaks; obstacle_delay_s~LogNormal(meanlog=-1.20,sdlog=0.35)
edges._comment: Geometric straight-line distance is 14.2 m; 15.0 m allows a mild detour around desks and seated students while remaining within the ±20% consistency target.

edges.travel_time_model: effective_speed_mps = min((period in ['morning_break','afternoon_break']) ? max_v_ms_congested : max_v_ms_normal, max(0.35, walk_speed_mps~Normal(mean=1.35,sd=0.18) / congestion_factor)); congestion_factor=1.0 lessons,1.15 arrival/end_of_day,1.10 lunch,1.80 short_breaks; obstacle_delay_s~LogNormal(meanlog=-1.20,sdlog=0.35)
edges._comment: Geometric straight-line distance is 12.4 m; the wider effective path on this route makes the realised travel distance close to straight-line.

edges.travel_time_model: effective_speed_mps = min((period in ['morning_break','afternoon_break']) ? max_v_ms_congested : max_v_ms_normal, max(0.35, walk_speed_mps~Normal(mean=1.35,sd=0.18) / congestion_factor)); congestion_factor=1.0 lessons,1.15 arrival/end_of_day,1.10 lunch,1.80 short_breaks; obstacle_delay_s~LogNormal(meanlog=-1.20,sdlog=0.35)
edges._comment: Geometric straight-line distance is 6.1 m; 7.1 m reflects a realistic weave between tables and bags and keeps the edge consistent with the supplied coordinates, which imply a shorter route than the rough 9 m brief estimate.

sku_database.name: Bananas

daily_distribution._comment: Mean is the expected total demand across both shelves combined on an operating weekday before the location split is applied.

school_period_profile._comment: Values sum to 1.0. Combined short-break share is intentionally dominant so the learned policy is rewarded for pre-break replenishment.

weekday_multiplier._comment: Friday is slightly softer and weekends are fully disabled because the pilot only runs Monday to Friday.

sku_database._comment: Fastest-moving fruit. At the primary shelf this demand profile is strong enough to push stock close to reorder after a busy break without forcing constant overstock of a perishable item.

sku_database._comment: Very close to bananas in popularity, but slightly smoother because citrus tends to keep longer and is less prone to same-day spoilage concerns.
